title: Extension by zero is exact and preserves punctual weights
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and the coefficient and weight conventions of [def-weil-punctual-weights], including $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and write $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ for its base change to $k$. Use the constructible hearts [def-weil-constructible-heart] and Weil structures [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The rational/common-stage compact-support functor [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] along $j$ sends constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves to constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves and induces an exact functor $j_!$ on these sheaves.
For every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, the coefficient fibre $(j_!\mathcal F)_{\bar x}$ is naturally $\mathcal F_{\bar u}$ if $\bar x=j\bar u$, and is zero if $\bar x$ lies outside $U$. Here coefficient fibres are the adic rational/common-stage fibres of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. At a closed point $x\in|X_0|$ lying in $U_0$, this identification intertwines the local geometric Frobenius operators of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].
Consequently, for every $w\in\mathbf R$, $j_!$ preserves punctual upper weight bounds (every local eigenvalue $\alpha$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|\le q_x^{w/2}$) and punctual $\iota$-purity of weight $w$ (the corresponding equality), where $q_x=\#\kappa(x)$ as in [def-weil-punctual-weights].

proof.text: For the auxiliary declaration zlOpenWeilPull_isRightAdjoint, use the existing common-stage open-heart adjunction with its prescribed underlying pullback [lem-zl-common-stage-open-heart-adjunction]. Geometric Frobenius and its inverse preserve the constructible heart by [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact]; their inverse equivalence is the normalized common-stage isomorphism transport [lem-pod-isomorphism-field-transport]. Thus the heart Frobenius functors are autoequivalences. The canonical heart square of [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category] has an invertible inverse mate [lem-stage3-inverse-mate-equivalences]. Lift the adjunction to invertible Frobenius algebras by [lem-sf-fixed-pair-adjunction-lift]. Explicitly identify an invertible algebra in the heart with a Weil object whose underlying carrier lies in the heart: both directions preserve the carrier, structure isomorphism and arrows. The normalization equation of the heart square identifies the resulting restriction functor with zlWeilPull. Transport the lifted adjunction through these equivalences. The main theorem uses the comparison steps below.

Retain the finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation of the common-stage open-heart left adjoint. Its Frobenius lift preserves them by the fixed-pair preservation instances; the heart-pair equivalences preserve all limits and colimits. Uniqueness of left adjoints transfers exactness to zlOpenWeilShriek. Finite products imply additivity.
Apply carrier realization to the canonical adjunction and each given integral finite-stage presentation.
Apply the natural geometric fibre comparison to the canonical adjunction.
Apply finite-stage Frobenius compatibility to the canonical adjunction.

For each eigenvalue of the output use spectrum transport to obtain an input closed point and the identical residue cardinality. Apply the input upper bound or purity equality at that point and rewrite the cardinality. The argument works for every real weight and every complex embedding.

reviewed_lean.note: Read the node, the dependency nodes, the report and all three delivered modules, plus the live declarations they use. Hypotheses match the node (separated finite-type k0-schemes, open immersion j0, l != p, Qbar with iota); quasi-compactness of j0 is derived, and no properness, Noetherian or universe restriction is added. j_! is the left adjoint of the recorded zlWeilPull on the sfCommonStageWeilSheaf hearts: canonical, not hollow, mathematically j_!. Conclusions present: exactness (additive, finite limits, finite colimits); carrier iso with sfQbarCompactSupportValue for (j,id) plus a natural finite-stage comparison with sfCompactSupportFiniteFunctor; natural fibre iso inside U and zero fibre outside U at every geometric point; natural closed-fibre iso intertwining localClosedFrobeniusCohomology at closed points of U0; preservation of upper bounds and purity for all real w with q_x = card of the residue field. Edge cases (empty U, identity immersion, zero sheaf, any w, eigenvalues outside the field of definition) are covered. Section 1(B) repairs are justified: the punctual-weights node is re-pointed from the old WeilSheaf predicates to the recorded heart and its definitions match the node; the adic-fibre node's new module re-exports the original, repeats its twelve clauses verbatim and adds the intrinsic fibre via purCoefficientModel. Item changes only in lean and stmt_deps (three landed nodes added, as the brief allows); statements verbatim; new names unique; docstrings, sorry-only proofs, imports and line lengths conform. nt_compile.py on the three snapshot files: clean, 4.3/3.6/11.2 s, reproduced twice. Minor notes only: landed citers still use the old upstream weight predicates (a stage-3 bridge); the Frobenius clause is stated on the recorded local-Frobenius fibre, which is where that operator lives.
